items.rationale: Drilling is glazing work under 1.3 (preparatory operation to receive the pane or its hardware). The description shows only accidental damage cover, with no glazing peril agreed, so 2.6.4, 3.5(b) and 7.1.11 exclude it, and t=0.

items.description: Installation of new glass into frame
items.rationale: Setting and fitting a glazing element is glazing work. Glass breakage is outside the accidental damage peril (2.6.4) and the optional peril 2.1(e) is not shown as agreed, so 3.5 excludes the line and t=0.
The replacement pane is the principal glazing item. Optional glazing breakage cover is not agreed, so 2.6.4 and 3.5(a) exclude it even though the same knock damaged covered timber parts, and t=0.

items.description: Repair of dented and gouged solid-wood door frame
items.rationale: The frame is a non-glazing part of the cabinet (4.2.2). It was dented and gouged by the knock, which is sudden accidental damage under 2.6.1, so the repair including finish is covered under 7.1.1(b). Estimated at a fair flat-rate market price.

items.description: Repair and refinish of scratched and chipped wooden shelf
items.rationale: The shelf was hit in the same incident and is an affected item, so repair and refinishing of the damaged part is covered under 7.1.1(b) and 2.6.2. Estimated at a fair flat-rate market price.

This is an attendance charge. Covered work (frame and shelf repair) was carried out at the visit, so one attendance is payable in full under 7.1.12 and is not reduced for the non-covered glazing work. Small service lines tend to be cheap.
